note_on_method: Nobody working on this has played on these courts. Every count, address, price, opening time and lighting statement comes from the City of Scottsdale's own pages — its pickleball page for the counts, addresses and hours, and each park's own page for the cost and the sharing rules. The City lists five locations and three are published here; the two that are not are named below with the reason, because "not listed" and "does not exist" are different things.

slots.parking: Scottsdale publishes nothing about parking at any of the three, which is the same gap every city in this directory has. What it does publish instead is more useful than most parking notes would be: the hours, the price, the lighting and the rule for sharing a court when someone is waiting. If you are driving to Horizon Park on a weekday morning — the time the City itself names as busiest — the thing to know is not where to park but that you may be rotating on after a 30-minute game rather than walking straight on. For what it is worth, all three are suburban parks in north and east Scottsdale rather than dense street-grid sites, but that is an observation about the map and not a fact from the City.
slots.peak_hours: This is the first city page in the directory where this section is written from a source rather than from inference. Scottsdale states it, in the same words, on each of the three park pages: "Mornings are typically the busiest time for pickleball play" at Cholla, at Horizon and at Thompson Peak. Eleven cities in, no other operator has published a peak time at all. The City pairs it with the rule that decides what a busy morning actually feels like — play is standard format, first to 11 and win by two, with a 30-minute time limit, "at which time players should rotate off the court with any waiting players". So a queue at 9 a.m. is a queue that moves. Nothing is reservable anywhere in Scottsdale: the City's pickleball page states that courts are first come, first served, that no reservation is required, and that no amplified sound is permitted.
slots.surface_condition: No surface is stated for any Scottsdale court, which is ordinary — only two cities in this directory have ever published one. What Scottsdale does publish is a piece of maintenance history you can act on: Thompson Peak Park's three courts were closed from 17 August to 11 September 2026 for resurfacing, and were expected to reopen on the 12th, weather permitting. That is a statement about work rather than about a material, so it appears in this city's court notes and not in the surface field. It is also the reason one of the three venues on this page is published as closed rather than as open — the City said so on the day we checked, and a directory that quietly drops that is less useful than one that repeats it.
slots.local_scene: Twenty-one verified courts across three parks, every one of them lit and every one of them free — Scottsdale is the first city in this directory where all three of count, lighting and cost are answered at every published venue. Horizon Park's ten courts are the largest single count here and among the larger ones anywhere on this site. What is most striking, though, is not the provision but the documentation: Scottsdale is the only operator we have read that tells you how to behave on a shared court, and the only one that tells you when the courts are busy. The City also runs a free public drop-in programme on Scottsdale Community College's six lighted courts, in partnership with the college — that venue is not published here because the Census places it outside the city limits, but it is real and it is free, and anyone playing in south Scottsdale should know it exists.

best_for.heading: Best if you want the most courts
best_for.text: Horizon Park has ten lighted courts, the largest count in Scottsdale and one of the larger sets anywhere in this directory. Free, drop-in, not reservable, open from sunrise to 10:30 p.m. daily. The City says mornings are typically busiest here, and the sharing rule that applies — 30-minute games, rotate off for anyone waiting — is what makes ten courts feel like ten rather than like four occupied ones.

best_for.heading: Best if you are playing in the evening
best_for.text: Any of them, honestly — all three published Scottsdale venues are lit and all three run to 10:30 p.m. Cholla Park is the pick if you want eight courts without Horizon's crowd: the City marks it "Eight outdoor lighted courts", free to use, drop-in and not reservable. In a city where summer daytime play is barely an option, sunrise-to-10:30 p.m. lighting at every venue is the single most valuable thing Scottsdale publishes.

best_for.heading: Best if you do not want to pay
best_for.text: Every published court in Scottsdale is free, and unusually the City says so rather than leaving it to be assumed: "They are free to use" appears on each park page. Across this whole directory only one other city has a verified free court — Portland — and only because Portland wrote the word down too. Cholla, Horizon and Thompson Peak are all free, all lit and all open sunrise to 10:30 p.m.

faqs.q: How many pickleball courts does Scottsdale have?
faqs.a: We have verified 21 across three City of Scottsdale venues: eight at Cholla Park, ten at Horizon Park and three at Thompson Peak Park. All are outdoor, all are lit and all are free. The City lists two further locations that are not on this page — Ashler Hills Park and Scottsdale Community College — for reasons set out below.

No, and you cannot. The City's pickleball page states that courts are available on a first come, first served basis and that no reservation is required. It also states that no amplified sound is permitted at any of these locations.

faqs.q: What happens if all the courts are taken?
faqs.a: You wait, and then you play — Scottsdale publishes the rule, which almost no operator does. Court use is limited to standard game format, first side to 11 points or leading by at least two, with a 30-minute time limit, "at which time players should rotate off the court with any waiting players". So the queue moves on a defined clock rather than on whoever is most assertive.

Mornings, at all three venues. The City states it on each park page: "Mornings are typically the busiest time for pickleball play" at Cholla, Horizon and Thompson Peak. This is the only city in this directory whose operator has published a peak time, so it is the only city page here where that answer is a fact rather than an inference.

Yes, and the City says so rather than leaving it to be assumed. Each park page states "They are free to use". That matters because this directory does not record a court as free unless an operator has written it down — municipal park courts usually are free, and "usually" is not something we will put in a field. Only Portland and Scottsdale have verified free courts on this site.

faqs.q: Why is Thompson Peak Park shown as closed?
faqs.a: Because the City says it is. All three of its pickleball courts were closed from Monday 17 August to Friday 11 September 2026 for resurfacing, and are expected to reopen on Saturday 12 September, weather permitting. This page was checked on 4 September, inside that window. Our build asserts that closure notice is still on the City's page, so when the courts reopen and the notice comes down, the build fails and someone updates this rather than leaving a stale warning.

faqs.q: Why aren't Ashler Hills Park and Scottsdale Community College listed?
faqs.a: Two different reasons. Ashler Hills has eight lighted courts and an address the Census geocoder cannot resolve — 32220 N. 74th Way returns no match, on the City's spelling or on three variants — and this site requires an address that resolves before it will publish a venue. Scottsdale Community College has six lighted courts that the City runs a free public drop-in programme on in partnership with the college, and the geocoder places 9000 E Chaparral Rd in no incorporated place at all: it is not inside Scottsdale city limits. A city running a programme somewhere does not move that somewhere into the city.

faqs.q: How do you know all this?
faqs.a: From the City of Scottsdale's own pages, snapshotted on 4 September 2026 and committed to the repository that builds this site, so every number here can be checked against the document it came from. The counts, addresses, lighting and hours come from the City's pickleball page; the price and the sharing rules come from each park's own page. Every fact carries its source and the date it was checked.
